title: Reload-recovery reclaim treats every error, including transient timeouts, as a terminal room end
test: tests/browser/host-reload-recovery.spec.mjs: 'a reclaim cut off twice by the connection is retried and the stored room is resumed' (failed before); 'a reclaim the server rejects as terminal ends the session at once and clears the record' and 'leaving the host page during the pause between reclaim attempts sends no further attempt' (guards, passed before). Unit tests: tests/hostRecovery.test.js (classifyReclaimFailure, reclaimRetryDelayMs, reclaimWithRetry, createCancellableWait)
proof: Holds. The spec starts its own server.js on claimed ports, seeds the record {code, hostToken, ingestMode} in sessionStorage and puts a page.routeWebSocket proxy between the page's Socket.IO connection and the server that counts reclaim-host frames and, per frame, forwards it, cuts the connection right after the emit (what a lost link or a timeout looks like to the client) or answers it as a server that still holds the room. Case: the first two reclaim-host frames lose the connection, the third is answered. On the unchanged client (vite build into a scratch dir) the page spent socketRequest's own two attempts on the first two, threw, and terminateHostSession ended the session: 'Resume Sharing' never appeared (Expected visible, element(s) not found, after 20 s) and the record was cleared. After the fix the third attempt is made after the 0.5 s pause, 'Resume Sharing' shows, exactly 3 reclaim-host frames were sent, every one with reloadRecovery true, and the record is still in sessionStorage. Q-002 (error shapes): socketRequest tags a failure with a phase ('connect', 'ack-timeout', 'disconnect-after-emit' for timeouts, a socket that never connected and a lost connection; 'server' for an answer). lib/socket.js answers every reclaim-host rejection that means the room is gone (invalid parameters, reload recovery not enabled, room not found or token invalid) with createRoomState(RECLAIM_REJECTED, ...), which carries terminal: true; the handler's catch-all answer ('Internal error') and the client-side timeouts and disconnects carry no terminal field. classifyReclaimFailure(err) is therefore 'terminal' exactly when err.terminal === true (the rule onReconnect already uses) and 'transient' for everything else, unknown errors included; a unit test builds the errors through the real socketRequest and the real createRoomState to pin this. Retries: reclaimWithRetry makes at most 10 attempts inside a 25 s window (the server holds the room 30 s from the old page's disconnect and the reload has used some of it), each attempt a single socketRequest with at most 5 s to connect and 5 s for the ack (less near the end of the window, never under 1 s: socketRequest treats 0 as its 15 s default), pauses 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, then 4 s, no pause that would end past the window; it waits for a disconnected socket through socketRequest's own connect wait. A terminal failure returns at once with no retry (guard test: exactly 1 frame, error shown, record cleared). Cancellation: the effect's cleanup sets the cancel flag and clears the pause timer through createCancellableWait.cancel(), which also wakes the waiter; nothing is sent after it and the reply of a request in flight is ignored. The timer lives in the effect run's closure rather than a shared ref, so StrictMode's replayed effect cancels the first run and cannot touch the second (unit test 'StrictMode's replayed effect...'). Mutation check: with the cancel flag forced to false the browser test 'leaving the host page during the pause...' fails (3 frames when leaving, 5 after waiting). The retries also stop when the host starts a room of their own on the page (startGuard.activeOperation), see the .md. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1028/1028); the new spec 4 of 4, and the 12 media-flow scenarios (port-shifted copy) and the two earlier host specs pass on the fixed build.

title: When reclaiming a stored OBS room fails, stopObsIngest is a no-op because ingestModeRef is still 'browser'
test: tests/browser/host-reload-recovery.spec.mjs: 'a stored OBS room that cannot be reclaimed stops OBS even though the page starts in browser mode' (failed before); the terminal-rejection test also asserts that a stored browser-mode room opens no OBS connection (passed before and after). Unit test: tests/hostRecovery.test.js 'shouldStopObsAfterFailedReclaim: a stored OBS room needs a stop, nothing else does'
proof: Holds. The spec seeds {code, hostToken, ingestMode: 'obs'}, stands in for OBS with page.routeWebSocket on ws://127.0.0.1:4455 (an obs-websocket v5 stub that answers the handshake and records every request), and lets the real server reject the reclaim (the room does not exist: terminal). On the unchanged client the page ended the session ('Create new room' shown, record cleared) but OBS received nothing: 'requests OBS received' Expected "StopStream", Received [] after 10 s, because terminateHostSession's stopObsIngest returned at ingestModeRef.current !== 'obs' (a fresh page starts in 'browser' and only a successful reclaim sets 'obs'). After the fix OBS receives StopStream and the record is cleared. Fix: shouldStopObsAfterFailedReclaim(stored) is true when stored.ingestMode === 'obs'; on a final failure HostView calls terminateHostSession(reason, { ingestMode: 'obs' }), which hands the mode to stopObsIngest(modeOverride), which uses the override instead of ingestModeRef (the ref is not set, since the sync effect would overwrite it). With no control channel on a fresh page that goes to the existing stopObsStream({ password: obsPasswordRef.current }) fallback, and a channel, if one exists, is still used first; exactly one stop is sent, not one from the override and one from the ref. A stored browser-mode room does not stop OBS (the terminal test asserts zero OBS connections). Transient failures keep the record and OBS running until the window ends; then the OBS stop is sent together with terminateHostSession. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1028/1028).
